issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee who defaults on rent for which the mortgagee is liable and thereby contributes to a rent sale cannot extinguish the mortgagor’s right of redemption by purchasing the property at that sale, even when the mortgagor also defaulted.
material_facts: The mortgage terms made the mortgagees liable for part of the rent of the consolidated holding, and the mortgagees defaulted on that liability; the mortgagor also defaulted on the rent for which he was liable.
The defaults led to a rent decree and an execution sale of the mortgaged property.
The first appellate court found that the auction purchasers had purchased for the benefit of the contesting mortgagees.
The mortgagees argued that the sale extinguished the right of redemption because the mortgagor’s default would have led to the sale even if the mortgagees had paid their share.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagees gained an advantage by using their position as mortgagees to acquire the property at the execution sale. Under section 90 of the Indian Trusts Act, they must hold that advantage for the benefit of the persons interested in the property, and the mortgagor’s right of redemption remains available. The appeal was allowed and the preliminary decree for redemption was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 90 of the Indian Trusts Act requires a qualified owner who gains an advantage by availing himself of that position, in derogation of the rights of others interested in the property, to hold the advantage for their benefit, subject to repayment of their proper share of expenses and indemnity for proper liabilities. A mortgagee’s contribution to bringing about a sale through failure to pay rent for which the mortgagee is liable is directly connected to the mortgagee’s position. The mortgagor’s concurrent default does not negate that contribution. The rule applies even where the mortgagee’s rent liability is less than the major portion of the rent; the Court left open the case of a liability so small that the property would not ordinarily be sold for it. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: redemption_suit and mortgagee_owed_rent_for_property and mortgagee_default_contributed_to_sale and mortgagee_or_beneficiary_acquired_property_at_sale

predicates.redemption_suit: The proceeding sought redemption of mortgaged property.
predicates.mortgagee_owed_rent_for_property: The mortgagee was responsible for paying rent for the property, in whole or in part.
predicates.mortgagee_default_contributed_to_sale: The mortgagee failed to pay rent for which the mortgagee was responsible, and that failure helped bring about the execution sale.
predicates.mortgagee_or_beneficiary_acquired_proper: The mortgagee, or a purchaser acting for the mortgagee’s benefit, acquired the property at the execution sale.
predicates.mortgagor_retains_right_to_redeem: The mortgagor’s right to redeem the property remains available.

issues.definition: When a mortgagee responsible for rent helps bring about an execution sale by failing to pay it and then acquires the property at that sale, the mortgagor retains the right to redeem, even if the mortgagor also defaulted.
